title: Does synthetic pre-training pay off on a microcontroller? Accuracy, latency and energy across two MCUs
abstract: arXiv:2611.19931v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Rendered images are cheap to label, but a microcontroller classifier must survive 8-bit integer (INT8) quantisation and compute correctly on the chip. Five models, from MobileNetV2 at 224 px to a 61K-parameter convolutional neural network (CNN), were fine-tuned on a six-class scene dataset with and without a synthetic stage, against thresholds fixed in advance, and deployed on an ESP32-S3 and an RP2040. With full real data the stage gave no detectable gain. For the main deployable model the INT8 difference was +0.312 percentage points (pp), its interval below the +1.6 pp gain recomputed from the source study; quantisation did not detectably change it, nor did model size. With 10% of the real data the stage paid off for the CNN, by +3.438 pp on one seed and +2.715 pp over three; its cause is open. On the ESP32-S3 the main model took 152.7 ms and 16.3 mJ above idle per inference, and adding the stage changed neither beyond preset bounds. T

translated_title: 合成预训练在微控制器上划算吗？跨两款MCU的准确率、延迟与能耗评估
translated_abstract: 渲染图像的标注成本低廉，但微控制器分类器必须经受8位整数（INT8）量化并在芯片上正确运行。本研究将五个模型——从224像素的MobileNetV2到一个61K参数的卷积神经网络（CNN）——在六类场景数据集上分别带与不带合成预训练阶段进行微调，对照预先设定的判定阈值，并部署到ESP32-S3和RP2040两款微控制器上。在拥有全部真实数据时，合成阶段未带来可检测的增益：对于主要可部署模型，INT8量化下的差异仅为+0.312个百分点（pp），低于从原始研究重新计算得出的+1.6个百分点增益；量化未显著改变这一结果，模型规模也未产生影响。当真实数据缩减至10%时，合成阶段对CNN产生了回报：单个随机种子下提升+3.438个百分点，三个种子下平均提升+2.715个百分点，其内在原因尚待探明。在ESP32-S3上，主要模型每次推理耗时152.7毫秒、较空闲状态多消耗16.3毫焦能量，而加入合成阶段对这两项指标的改变均未超出预设界限。
tldr: 本研究在两款微控制器上系统评估了合成数据预训练的真实收益，发现在完整真实数据下几乎无增益（INT8差异仅+0.312个百分点），但在真实数据缩减至10%时可为小模型CNN带来约+2.7个百分点的提升，且不影响推理延迟与能耗，表明合成预训练的价值主要体现在真实数据稀缺的场景。
en_tdlr: This study systematically evaluates synthetic pre-training on two microcontrollers across accuracy, latency, and energy, finding no detectable gain with full real data (only +0.312 pp under INT8) but a ~+2.7 pp improvement for a small CNN when real data drops to 10%, with no measurable impact on latency or energy—indicating synthetic pre-training pays off mainly when real data is scarce.
